transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's so nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I came in because... gosh, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's just... I've been having this feeling like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, but even when I'm completely worn out—and I really should just be sitting still and resting—I get this feeling like I just have to jump up and do the next thing. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit I can't just relax, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way for you.
When you feel this need to jump up and keep moving, is it usually because your mind is filled with worries or concerns about various things in your life?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I don't think it's that. I hope it's okay to say, but I'm really not much of a worrywart. I try very hard to look on the bright side and not fret over things, you know? 

It's more just... even when everything is perfectly fine and I have absolutely nothing to be concerned about, I still get that... that buzzing feeling where I just can't stay put. It's not my thoughts making me anxious or anything like that, it's just my body wanting to go. 

I hope I'm not confusing things... is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you have these episodes of feeling like you need to keep moving, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual to feel fully rested?

Oh, heavens no. Um... I definitely still need my sleep. Even when I have that... that fidgety feeling during the day, I still get tired just like anyone else. I certainly wouldn't feel rested if I only got a few hours of sleep, that's for sure. 

I try my very best to get a full night's rest every night, so I definitely don't feel like I need less sleep than usual. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers so I can be helpful to you.
When you have this buzzing feeling in your body, do you find that moving your legs or walking around specifically helps to make the sensation go away, even if only for a little while?

Oh, um... I don't think so? I mean, I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to. It's not really like a cramp or a tickle in my legs that goes away if I stretch or take a little walk. 

Even if I do get up and start bustling around the house, doing chores or what have you, that... that humming feeling is still right there with me. It doesn't really turn off or feel relieved just because I'm moving my legs. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying my very best to explain it properly for you. I just wouldn't want to say yes and lead you down the wrong path. Is that the sort of thing you were looking for?

Looking back at your life, can you recall feeling this same kind of restless, buzzing energy when you were a child or a teenager, or is this something that only started more recently in your adult life?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose it's not entirely new. Um... I hope it's alright to admit this, but I've always been a bit of a... a handful, I guess you could say. 

Even way back in grade school, I remember my report cards always said similar things. The teachers were very kind, they always said I was a bright girl, but... well, they'd write that I was a bit careless. I was always misplacing my assignments, or I'd get too excited and talk out of turn in class. And, oh dear, they were always having to remind me to stay in my seat or just focus on finishing my work. 

I was just such an eager little thing, always wanting to be doing something else. I hope I'm not painting a terrible picture of myself! I really did try to be a good student. Does that help answer your question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing.
